text: You can run the sharing service yourself, on one Linux server with Docker Compose: the service, Caddy for the certificate, and a TURN relay.
First, point two DNS names at the server: one for the service, one for TURN.
Open ports 80 and 443 for Caddy, 3478 UDP for TURN, and the relay range.
Copy the example settings to a file called dot env, and fill in the release, both domains, the server's address and a random TURN secret.
This is a real run on a laptop, so both domains point at this machine here.
Docker compose up pulls the release image and starts all three.
Docker compose ps shows them running.
Check that it answers: health says ok, and web viewer dot json says which release runs.
The server's log has one line per event, such as a viewer joining or a wrong code.
Last, everyone enters your domain under Sharing service, in SpecDeck's Settings.
Your own sharing service, in a few commands.
